title: Pioneer Clinical Eval Matrix & Benchmarks Workshop
summary: Workshop focused on defining the quality evaluation matrix for the Pioneer Clinical POC. Agreed on golden prompt set construction, regression playlists, hallucination detection approach, scoring rubric (weighted metrics), and a concrete 4-week POC timeline with load/latency targets. SE (Maya) committed to a benchmark plan; AE (Alex) to share pricing and pilot SOW. Security questions on VPC/KMS and audit logs noted; CISO requested SOC2 artifacts and a short threat model doc.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time — Alex from Redwood Inference. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Dr. Leena Kapoor: Hi, Leena here.
[00:09] Samir Desai: Samir, platform.
[00:11] Hannah Ortiz: Hannah, data ops.
[00:13] Mark Liu: Mark, security.
[00:16] Alex Chen: Great. We want to nail down the eval matrix so the POC proves the system meets your accuracy and compliance needs, and that we measure cost/latency. Maya — do you want to frame the QA approach?
[00:22] Maya Patel: Sure. The idea is two parallel tracks: quality (golden prompts, regression playlists, hallucination and format checks) and performance (latency, throughput, token cost). For golden prompts we want a small curated set — 100 to 200 prompts — that represent high-value clinical flows, e.g., discharge summary extraction, adverse event normalization, and triage note generation.
[00:38] Dr. Leena Kapoor: Quick question: are these prompts static or will we include paraphrases? We need to ensure robustness not just memorization.
[00:44] Jonah Rivera: Great point. Recommend 3 tiers: canonical prompt, 3 paraphrases, and noisy variants (typos, truncated context). That lets us check robustness and hallucination under realistic inputs.
[00:56] Samir Desai: For workload sizing, here's our current traffic snapshot — about 500 daily NLP jobs, spiking to 2000 during morning triage. Typical output token length is ~120 tokens; average input is 180 tokens. We want the POC to hit 100 req/s sustained for a 10-minute window to simulate peak concurrency.
[01:15] Alex Chen: Okay 100 req/s with ~120 tokens out — that maps to ~12k tokens per second outgoing. We'll propose runner configs: hosted mode default, and a dedicated pool for side-by-side test if you want. What's your tolerance for latency?
[01:26] Dr. Leena Kapoor: 95th percentile under 350ms for single-turn generation is ideal; 99th under 700ms acceptable for complex calls. If latency is too high we risk employee workflow degradation.
[01:36] Maya Patel: We'll record p50/p95/p99 and end-to-end time including pre/post processing. Also will check token-level CPU vs GPU times.
[01:43] Mark Liu: From security, VPC peering + customer KMS is mandatory for pilot. We also need data retention controls — can you guarantee zero retention for PII?
[01:50] Alex Chen: Yes we support customer-managed KMS and retention policies. We'll share the SOC2 whitepaper and an architecture sketch. Note: private deployment available if air-gapped requirement emerges.
[01:59] Hannah Ortiz: Back to quality — what about hallucination detection? We need automated heuristics and a human-in-loop threshold.
[02:05] Maya Patel: We propose two mechanisms: 1) Reference-based checks when ground-truth exists — exact matches, semantic similarity (embedding cosine thresholds), and 2) model-based verification prompts: ask model to assert sources or return structured citations. Also a classifier trained on past hallucination cases to flag suspicious outputs. For scoring, we'd weight format correctness 40%, factuality 35%, latency 15%, token cost 10%.
[02:28] Dr. Leena Kapoor: Weighted scoring sounds good. How do you operationalize format checks for e.g., structured fields (ICD codes) vs free text?
[02:35] Jonah Rivera: We'll use a combination: schema validation for structured outputs (regex, enum checks) and classifiers for free text structure. Failures will be categorized: hard format failure (missing required fields), soft (minor mismatch), hallucination (invented entities).
[02:48] Samir Desai: On regression tests — we want a weekly regression playlist triggered after model swaps. That playlist should contain our golden prompts + 500 synthetic cases pulled from production (anonymized). Failures should block rollout if quality delta > 5% on weighted score.
[03:04] Maya Patel: We'll instrument baseline runs and then run A/B and canary tests. Canary could be 5% traffic for 24–48 hours and automated rollback if regression threshold exceeded.
[03:14] Dr. Leena Kapoor: How do we measure hallucination rate? A manual review sample or automated?
[03:18] Maya Patel: Both. For the POC we'll do automated detectors to tag likely hallucinations, then a human audit on a stratified sample (e.g., 200 cases). For production, you can build a periodic human audit cadence.
[03:28] Mark Liu: From compliance, we need audit logs per token and per-request metadata for six months for the POC. Cost for storing that?
[03:34] Alex Chen: We'll estimate storage delta. For the POC we'll include 90-day logs in the quoted pilot SOW; longer retention is an add-on.
[03:40] Samir Desai: Benchmarks — we need cost-per-1M tokens at our expected profile. Can you provide cost projections for baseline models and quantized variants?
[03:47] Alex Chen: Yes. We'll run benchmarks against two model families: an open foundation model (quantized 4-bit) and a higher-accuracy variant. We'll provide tokenized cost, measured latency p95, and throughput at target batch sizes. Expect different cost/latency tradeoffs; we'll present a recommended tradeoff curve.
[04:03] Dr. Leena Kapoor: Timeline — what does a concise POC look like?
[04:07] Alex Chen: Propose 4-week plan: Week 0 (kickoff & access), Week 1 (golden prompt set + baseline runs), Week 2 (benchmark perf & load testing), Week 3 (regression playlist and hallucination audits), Week 4 (final report, SOW/pricing and next steps). Could compress to 3 weeks if Pioneer provides quick access to anonymized samples.
[04:26] Hannah Ortiz: We can deliver anonymized samples within 5 business days. Also we need reproducible eval scripts so our engineers can run them in-house.
[04:33] Maya Patel: We'll share a reproducible harness (pytest style) and a Jupyter notebook for quick checks.
[04:38] Samir Desai: Acceptance criteria — spell it out.
[04:42] Alex Chen: Proposed POC success criteria: 1) Weighted quality score >= 88% on golden prompts, 2) Hallucination rate < 1.5% on audited sample, 3) Format adherence >= 95% for structured outputs, 4) P95 latency < 350ms under target load, 5) Cost projection within agreed threshold (we'll show cost per 1M tokens < $X — TBD). If three out of five pass and the remaining are planable improvements, consider partial success.
[05:10] Dr. Leena Kapoor: We need to define how you compute 'hallucination rate' precisely.
[05:14] Maya Patel: For POC: hallucination = any invented clinically significant entity (e.g., drug, diagnosis) not supported by input or ground-truth. The human audit will confirm. We'll provide the audit criteria and examples up front.
[05:27] Mark Liu: Also request encryption at rest and in transit details, plus penetration testing schedule.
[05:31] Alex Chen: Noted. We'll send SOC2, encryption whitepaper, and an outline of our pen-test cadence. We'll accept an NDA addendum if needed.
[05:40] Hannah Ortiz: About golden prompts — can Redwood help craft them? We can provide 20 seed cases.
[05:45] Jonah Rivera: Absolutely. We'll take your 20 seeds and expand via paraphrasing + noisy variants to reach ~150 canonical variants and then split into a weekly regression playlist. We'll also pick 30 'edge-case' prompts for hallucination stress tests.
[05:58] Dr. Leena Kapoor: For scoring approach, can you show an example calculation?
[06:03] Maya Patel: Example: For a single prompt — format correct (1/1) -> 100% * 0.4 = 40 points; factuality similarity 0.92 -> 0.92 * 35 = 32.2; latency normalized (p50 120ms -> within target) -> 15 points; cost normalized -> 8 points. Total ~95.2/100. We'll provide the spreadsheet so you can tweak weights.
[06:23] Samir Desai: What about edge-case hallucination detection where model hallucinates plausible but incorrect ICD codes?
[06:28] Maya Patel: We'll add rule-based validators for ICD code ranges and cross-check using external lookup tables as a first defense. Suspicious codes flagged require human confirmation.
[06:36] Mark Liu: Can Redwood sign an agreement to not use our data for model training?
[06:39] Alex Chen: Yes, we offer contractual clauses: no training on customer data for hosted plans; for private/dedicated we can guarantee separation. We'll put that in the SOW.
[06:48] Dr. Leena Kapoor: For regression playlist size — you mentioned 500 synthetic cases from production. How will you anonymize?
[06:52] Hannah Ortiz: We can run a prescripted anonymization pipeline and deliver hash-only IDs.
[06:57] Maya Patel: We'll give you the transformation scripts so you can run locally and we'll only receive anonymized texts.
[07:03] Alex Chen: Any blockers from Pioneer side?
[07:06] Samir Desai: Need legal signoff on data processing and quick SOC2 review. Also resource allocation from our ML infra team for the first week.
[07:12] Mark Liu: I'll need the threat model and pen-test schedule before we allow any VPC peering.
[07:18] Alex Chen: We'll prepare a short threat model doc and share SOC2 artifacts by EOD Friday.
[07:23] Dr. Leena Kapoor: Great. I want a one-page acceptance checklist — can you produce that?
[07:27] Alex Chen: Yes, a single-page POC acceptance checklist that maps directly to the five success criteria.
[07:31] Jonah Rivera: About benchmarks — we'll run two scenarios: steady-state 100 req/s and spike test 300 req/s for 2 minutes. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, error rate, and warmup behavior.
[07:44] Samir Desai: Will you simulate upstream preprocessing latency? Our pipeline adds ~40ms on average.
[07:48] Maya Patel: We'll add a synthetic 40ms upstream delay in the harness so E2E numbers match your stack.
[07:53] Hannah Ortiz: On deliverables — we need reproducible scripts, raw logs for our audit, a report with plots, and the evaluation spreadsheet.
[07:59] Alex Chen: Affirmative. We'll hand over harness, raw logs (anonymized), and final report with recommendations.
[08:05] Dr. Leena Kapoor: Any concerns about model drift during POC?
[08:08] Maya Patel: We'll pin the model version in the sandbox and record checksums; regression playlists will detect drift.
[08:14] Samir Desai: If the model underperforms, what's the remediation path?
[08:17] Alex Chen: We'll propose immediate mitigations: prompt tuning, temperature adjustments, or switching to a different model variant; and for long-term, fine-tuning or retrieval augmentation.
[08:25] Mark Liu: We want a performance SLA for Dedicated if we move to that.
[08:29] Alex Chen: Dedicated offerings include SLA-backed latency/throughput — we'll include targets in the dedicated proposal.
[08:34] Dr. Leena Kapoor: Okay let's recap next steps before we close.
[08:37] Alex Chen: Recap: Redwood to produce: 1) POC SOW & pricing, 2) SOC2 + encryption + pen-test cadence docs, 3) reproducible eval harness and example notebooks, 4) draft golden prompt expansion (based on your 20 seeds), 5) threat model sketch. Pioneer to provide: 1) anonymized sample set within 5 business days, 2) legal contact for DPA, 3) infra contact to allocate resources.
[08:59] Samir Desai: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:02] Dr. Leena Kapoor: Thanks — looking forward.
